failures.evidence: `cd packages/envoy && go test -count=1 -run TestNoSessionLineNamesAHostOrAStoreID ./cmd/agent-secrets/` FAILS at this head with 8 failing subtests (`--- FAIL: TestNoSessionLineNamesAHostOrAStoreID (6.64s)`, `FAIL github.com/sjawhar/envoy/cmd/agent-secrets`). The same command on main, in a clone at f29f58b, PASSES — I ran it there and only the pty test below failed. So this change broke it. The test (cmd/agent-secrets/source_test.go:342-399) is main's invariant that no line a session's forms print names a host, an account, a region or a project: it asserts the output contains none of the broker's host, `127.0.0.1`, the AWS account id, the region or 'the broker at'. The eight failures are the `request PENDING_ME` and `PENDING_ME --wait 200ms -- sh -c ...` forms of all four store kinds, each printing `waiting for ada@example.com to approve it on the secrets broker: http://127.0.0.1:37931/approve/rec-pending-1`, whose host the invariant forbids. This is not a flake and not the pod: it reproduces every run, needs no Postgres, and is green on main. It has been red since the branch first printed the broker's page URL rather than only this round — the round-2 code called `waitingOn(approver, approveURL)` and printed `*approveURL` the same way [INFERENCE from reading the round-2 source; the measured facts are that it is red at 6fb80d4ede9e and green at f29f58b]. No round of mine caught it earlier because the plan's A8 row calls the cmd/agent-secrets tests CI's (gVisor), and CI has not settled on this branch yet; the lane that would catch it, `envoy-go`, was still queued at 15:33Z. The pin already exists in the repository, so I wrote no test of my own. Resolving it needs a judgement rather than a one-line change, and it belongs to the implementer with the architect: spec A12 requires `agent-secrets` to print the broker's page URL while it waits, and that URL necessarily names the broker's host, which main's invariant forbids for every line. Either that invariant gets an explicit carve-out for the approval page's own URL, written into the test and its comment, or the printed line names the page some other way. The invariant's other members — the account id, the region, the project, 'the broker at' — are untouched either way.

observationsForTheReviewer: Not a failure, since no broker reaches it: packages/envoy/cmd/agent-secrets/main.go dereferences `*result.RecordID` in three places (lines 720, 766 and 962) for a request whose state is pending, and RecordID is `*string` in both the client's and the broker's own models (client.go:250,304; handlers_ui_records.go's requests row, whose record_id column is nullable). A pending request always carries one today — insertRequest's comment says a pending row's record_id is filled in by createPending in the same transaction — so the nil case is unreachable against this broker and against main's. It is worth a nil check all the same, because the whole point of that code path is to tolerate a broker older than this change.

The approval page's routes now spend the account class's per-address bucket (DefaultAccountLimit, 50/s with a burst of 200). I could not make a person's browsing hit it: 1200 reads of GET /signin/status from this pod in 22 s were all 200, because the pod cannot drive curl faster than the bucket refills. So the refusal itself is the unit tests' and CI's; what I can report is that ordinary use is not refused. One thing for the operator rather than for this pull request: with a load balancer in front and BROKER_TRUSTED_PROXY_HEADER unset, every browser and Dispatch's ServiceAccount share one address's bucket.

Still true from earlier rounds, and still not a failure: a signed-in person of the domain who is not the approver is served the whole record page — the secret names, the requesting enrollment, the reason and the times — with no decision form. The spec's design describes that page, and A2 requires only that she decide nothing, which she does not.
